quote.after:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the general absolutely continuous curve calculus and its fundamental theorem. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a strongly causal time-oriented smooth Lorentzian
four-manifold ([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause
(b)) and let $h$ be a smooth positive definite metric on $M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Then for every compact set
$K\subseteq M$ there is $L(K)\in[0,\infty)$ such that
$$\ell_h(\gamma)\le L(K)$$
for every future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]) with $\gamma([a,b])\subseteq K$.

Consequently, if $\gamma$ is parametrized by $h$-arclength
($\ell_h(\gamma|_{[s,t]})=t-s$) and its image is contained in the compact set
$K$, then $b-a\le L(K)$.

after.claim: (Compact enclosure of the joining curves.) If $p_k=q_k$ for all $k$ in an infinite set, then passing to that subsequence and using uniqueness of limits gives $p=q$, so $p\le q$ by reflexivity; the claim is then proved. Hence, passing to a subsequence, we may assume $p_k\ne q_k$ for all $k$, and choose a future causal curve $\gamma_k:[0,1]\to M$ with $\gamma_k(0)=p_k$, $\gamma_k(1)=q_k$ for each $k$. Choose $\varepsilon>0$ so small that $p^-:=\exp_p(-\varepsilon N_p)$ and $q^+:=\exp_q(\varepsilon N_q)$ are defined; by [L4], $p^-\ll p$ and $q\ll q^+$. Since $I^+(p^-)$ and $I^-(q^+)$ are open and contain $p$, respectively $q$ [L1], there is $k_0$ with $p_k\in I^+(p^-)$ and $q_k\in I^-(q^+)$ for $k\ge k_0$. Fix such a $k$. For every point $x$ of the image of $\gamma_k$ one has $p_k\le x\le q_k$, so $p^-\le x$ and $x\le q^+$ by transitivity [L1]; hence $$\gamma_k([0,1])\subseteq D:=J^+(p^-)\cap J^-(q^+),$$ and $D$ is compact by [L1].

(Bounded reparametrizations.) Let $\alpha_k:[0,L_k]\to M$ be $\gamma_k$ reparametrized by $h$-arclength, so $L_k=\ell_h(\gamma_k)$, $\alpha_k(0)=p_k$ and $\alpha_k(L_k)=q_k$. By step 1.1 and [L2], $L_k\le L(D)<\infty$ for all $k\ge k_0$; in particular the sequence $L_k$ is bounded and has a convergent subsequence, with limit $b\le L(D)$.

(Closedness.) Passing to a subsequence, $L_k\to b<\infty$; by [L3] there is a future causal curve $\alpha:[0,b]\to M$ with $\alpha(0)=p$, $\alpha(b)=q$ to which a subsequence converges uniformly. If $b>0$ then $\alpha$ is a future causal curve from $p$ to $q$, so $p\le q$; if $b=0$ then [L3] gives $p=q$, so again $p\le q$. This proves the closedness of $\le$.

(Closedness of the cones.) Let $y_j\to y$ with $y_j\in J^+(K)$ for a compact $K$: choose $x_j\in K$ with $x_j\le y_j$. Passing to a subsequence, $x_j\to x\in K$ because $K$ is compact, so step 3.1 applied to $x_j\le y_j$ gives $x\le y$, that is, $y\in J^+(K)$; hence $J^+(K)$ is closed. The same argument with the order reversed shows that $J^-(K)$ is closed, and with $K=\{x\}$ this gives closedness of $J^\pm(x)$.

(Compact truncated cones.) Let $K_1,K_2$ be compact. For each $x\in K_1$ choose $\varepsilon_x>0$ with $x^-:=\exp_x(-\varepsilon_xN_x)$ defined; by [L4] $x^-\ll x$, so $\{I^+(x^-)\}_{x\in K_1}$ is an open cover of $K_1$ [L1] and has a finite subcover $I^+(x^-_1),\dots,I^+(x^-_m)$ with $x_i\in K_1$. If $y\in J^+(K_1)$, choose $x\in K_1$ with $x\le y$ and $i$ with $x\in I^+(x^-_i)$; then $x^-_i\le x\le y$, so $y\in J^+(x^-_i)$. Hence $J^+(K_1)\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^mJ^+(x^-_i)$. Likewise, applying the time reverse, $K_2$ is covered by finitely many sets $I^-(y^+_j)$ with $y_j\in K_2$ and $J^-(K_2)\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^nJ^-(y^+_j)$. Therefore $$J^+(K_1)\cap J^-(K_2)\subseteq\bigcup_{i,j}\bigl(J^+(x^-_i)\cap J^-(y^+_j)\bigr),$$ a finite union of compact causal diamonds, hence compact by [L5]; and $J^+(K_1)\cap J^-(K_2)$ is closed by step 4.1. A closed subset of a compact set is compact [L5], so $J^+(K_1)\cap J^-(K_2)$ is compact.
